segments.say: Now imagine a small hourglass, sitting on a wooden shelf beside your bed. In the dim light, you can just see the sand inside, pale and fine, trickling slowly from the top into the bottom. A thin, steady stream. Grain after grain after grain. It doesn't rush, and it doesn't stop. It simply falls, softly, the way it always has.

Picture the hourglass in the candlelight. Its wooden frame, smooth with age. The glass, clear and curved. And the sand inside, falling in a fine, silent thread, gathering in a small soft hill at the bottom. You could watch it for a long time. There's something very calming about it, the way it measures time without ticking, without any sound at all.

Watch the sand for a while, in your mind. A thin stream, falling. And as you watch, let your breath slow down to match it. Soft, steady, unhurried. The sand doesn't worry about how much is left. It just keeps falling, one grain at a time. And you don't need to worry about anything either. Just breathe, and watch, and rest.

Here's a thought for the night. One grain at a time. That's how the sand falls, and that's how time passes too. Not in great rushes, but in small, gentle moments, one after another. Tonight, you only need to live this one. This breath. This grain. And then the next will come, softly, on its own, without you needing to do anything at all.

Now imagine a tree just outside your window. An old, wide tree, with strong branches. You've watched it through the seasons, though perhaps you've never really noticed. Let's watch it now, slowly, through a whole year. Not rushing through the months, but letting each season unfold gently, one after another, like pages in a quiet book.

It's spring. The branches are still bare, but if you look closely, you can see tiny buds appearing at the tips, pale green and tightly curled. Day by day, they swell. Then one soft morning, they begin to open, and small, bright leaves unfold. A bird comes to sit on a branch, and sings. The air smells of rain and new grass.

Now it's summer. The tree is full and green, its leaves thick and wide, rustling softly in the warm breeze. It casts a deep, cool shade on the grass below. On hot afternoons, the light filters through the leaves in shifting patterns. At night, the leaves whisper in the dark. The tree seems to breathe, slowly, in and out, along with the summer.

Now it's autumn. Picture the tree, glowing gold and amber in the late afternoon light. A few leaves let go, and drift slowly down, turning in the air before they settle on the grass. The breeze is cooler now. The light is softer. And the tree seems calm and unhurried, letting go of its leaves one by one, without any fuss.

Just like the tree, you can let go of things tonight, gently, one by one. Let go of a worry from the day. Watch it drift down, like a leaf, and settle on the grass. Let go of a thought you've been carrying. Let it float away. The tree doesn't hold on to its leaves forever. It knows they'll grow again in spring. And so will everything you need.

Let's watch the whole year of the tree together. Spring, with its small green buds. Summer, with its wide canopy of leaves. Autumn, glowing gold, and letting go. And winter, bare and resting. Each season is slow. Each one takes its time. And together, they make a full and gentle year, every part of it worth noticing.

Now it's winter. The tree stands bare against the pale sky, its branches dark and quiet. Snow settles along them, in thin white lines. The tree isn't sad, and it isn't empty. It's simply resting. Deep inside, it's gathering strength, quietly, for the spring to come. Winter is the tree's long, peaceful sleep.

And you can rest like the tree tonight. Still and quiet. Not doing anything. Just gathering strength, slowly and deeply, for the day to come. There's nothing wrong with resting. It's not wasted time. It's how living things grow. The tree knows this, and your body knows it too. So let yourself rest, as deeply as the tree in winter.

Here's a gentle reminder. Rest is part of the year, too. The quiet winters, the slow evenings, the nights of deep sleep. They're not gaps in our lives. They're part of what makes the rest of it possible. So tonight, you don't need to make the most of anything. You only need to rest, and let the night take care of you.

show.text: Rest is part of the year, too.

segments.say: Back on the shelf by your bed, the hourglass is still falling. Slowly. Softly. The little hill of sand at the bottom has grown a little higher. The stream from the top is still thin and steady. Time is passing, gently, the way it always does. And you're lying here, warm and heavy and calm, letting it pass, with nothing to worry about at all.

Let your breath slow down a little more. In, softly. Out, even more softly. In. And out. Each breath like a grain of sand, falling into place. Each one a little calmer than the last. Your body is heavy. Your mind is quiet. And sleep is very close now, like a warm blanket being drawn gently up over your shoulders.

In a moment, if you're still awake, we'll take another gentle journey together, on a slow night train through a sleeping countryside. You won't need to do anything. Just sit by the window, and watch the dark landscape slide by. But there's no rush to get there. Take another slow breath first. In. And out. And let the train come to you.
